q: tell me about the Silk Road
a: The Silk Road was a network of ancient trade routes connecting China, Central Asia, India, Persia, the Arabian Peninsula, and the Mediterranean from around 130 BCE to the 15th century CE. It facilitated the exchange of goods (silk, spices, tea, porcelain, glass, textiles, precious metals), ideas (Buddhism spread from India to China, Nestorian Christianity to China, Islam across Central Asia), and technologies (papermaking, gunpowder, the compass, printing spread from China westward). The name comes from the lucrative Chinese silk trade. It was not a single road but a complex web of overland and maritime routes stretching over 6,400 km. The Silk Road declined after the 15th century due to the rise of maritime trade routes and the collapse of the Mongol Empire.
